topic: Exploring the 2-adic Metric: Where Infinite Sums Behave Differently

sections.title: The Familiar World: Real Convergence
lecture_lines: Standard metrics measure distance on a number line.
Convergence implies getting closer to a limit value.
Small steps result in finite, predictable sums.
animations: Fade in title 'Real Convergence' in #FFFFFF color.
Display standard sequence a_n = 1/n converging to 0 using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg].
Highlight limit point 0 in #FF0000 color. (Line 3 color change)

sections.title: Introducing the 2-adic Metric
lecture_lines: High powers of two mean smaller values.
animations: Fade in title '2-adic Metric' in #FFFFFF color.
Highlight the exponent v_2 in #00FF00 color [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]. (Line 3 color change)

sections.title: Surprising Sums: Convergence in 2-adic
lecture_lines: Infinite sums can diverge in standard calculus.
Partial sums of powers of two converge.
This series actually approaches negative one.
animations: Fade in title '2-adic Sums' in #FFFFFF color.
Show geometric series 1+2+4+8+... appearing. (Line 2 color change)
Show partial sums S_n converging 2-adically to -1. (Line 3 color change)
Highlight result -1 in #0000FF color. (Line 4 color change)
Show animation of nested 2-adic balls [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ball.svg]. (Line 5 color change)

sections.title: Key Properties: The Ultrametric Inequality
lecture_lines: Triangles behave more like nested hierarchies.
Numerical value is secondary to divisibility.
animations: Fade in title 'Ultrametric Inequality' in #FFFFFF color.
Display inequality d(x,z) <= max(d(x,y), d(y,z)). (Line 2 color change)
Animate points x, y, z forming an ultrametric triangle. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg] (Line 3 color change)

sections.title: Synthesis and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Distance definitions fundamentally reshape mathematical behavior.
Convergence relies on the underlying metric space.
Different metrics reveal new mathematical truths.
